prompt: What is the range of $y = \arccos(x)$ — that is, which angles can it return?
hint: For an inverse to exist, we chop the original graph down to a stretch that passes the horizontal line test.

hints.text: For an inverse to exist, we chop the original graph down to a stretch that passes the horizontal line test.
For cosine, the chosen stretch runs from the very top of the wave to the very bottom, with no repeats.
That stretch is $0^\circ$ to $180^\circ$, so those are the only angles $\arccos$ ever returns.

explanation: Cosine hits the same value many times, so we restrict it before inverting.
The agreed piece is $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$: cosine slides steadily from $1$ down to $-1$ there, hitting each value exactly once.
So $\arccos$ returns angles from $0^\circ$ to $180^\circ$ — its outputs cover quadrants I and II.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare the three inverses
steps: $\arctan$ returns strictly between $-90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ (quadrants IV and I). Only $\arccos$ can hand back an obtuse angle.
